ranking.name: Qwen3.8-27B
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp server, ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 (CUDA 12.8.1), --jinja, -ngl all, -fa on, -c 65536, -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0, -np 1, --no-mmproj, -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1
ranking.checkpoint: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF UD-Q3_K_XL (13.15 GB), fully on GPU, about 15.2 GiB VRAM
ranking.reason:
It has the strongest independent agentic evidence in the set. Artificial Analysis measured Terminal-Bench 2.1 at 79.8% (xhigh) and 65.2% (medium). The vendor reports TB2.1 73.0 and SWE-bench Pro 61.7. It is a dense model and fits entirely in VRAM with 64k context. Tool calls use the Qwen3-Coder XML parser in llama.cpp, and thinking can be toggled. Inferred decode speed is about 40-45 tok/s.

Caveats from the challenge records:
- Add the CUDA-graph hang workaround. Issue #27330 was reproduced on driver 595.99.02.
- q8_0 KV may slow decode (#27623; fix PR #31802 still open). If speed drops below 15 tok/s, fall back to f16 KV at a shorter context.
- Quality loss at Q3 is unmeasured.
- AA measured only 5.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, so it is not strong on the hardest tasks.
- vLLM cannot run it: the smallest build is 15.59 GiB.

ranking.name: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp server, server-cuda-b12407, --jinja, -ngl 99, --n-cpu-moe 21-22 (or rely on --fit), -c 131072 f16 KV, -fa on, -np 1, -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1
ranking.checkpoint: ggml-org/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF Q4_K_M (19.13 GiB). About 14.5 GiB VRAM and about 9 GiB of experts in RAM.
ranking.reason:
Its independent evidence is strong. NVIDIA's same-harness table gives SWE-bench Verified 70.12 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 44.38, the highest TB2.1 in that table. The vendor reports SWE-V 73.4 and TB2.0 51.5, and evaluated SkillsBench through OpenCode. KV cost is small (20 KiB/token), so 128k context is affordable. Inferred decode is about 40-90 tok/s.

Corrections and caveats:
- The GPU margin at --n-cpu-moe 20 is only 0.3-0.8 GiB, so use 21-22.
- Use server-cuda, not server-cuda13: the cuda13 image has a GeForce start-check risk.
- For precise coding, sample at temp 0.6 with presence 0. General thinking runs at temp 1.0 with presence 1.5.
- llama.cpp #30118: a missing <tool_call> opener can leak tool calls into content.
- vLLM is blocked on 16 GB (bug #66264).

ranking.checkpoint: unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF UD-IQ4_XS (35.79 GiB). About 13.2 GiB VRAM and about 25.7 GiB of experts in RAM.
ranking.reason:
This is the best non-thinking model with tools. Artificial Analysis independently measured tau2 79.5% and Terminal-Bench 2.1 38.2%. The vendor reports SWE-V 70.6-71.3 and Aider Polyglot 66.2. Tool calls use native Qwen3-Coder XML. Inferred decode is about 30-50 tok/s, bound by DDR5 bandwidth.

Corrections and caveats:
- Use the CUDA 12.8 image. The cuda13 image may refuse to start on GeForce, and #28581 reports IQ-quant miscompiles under nvcc 13.2.0 and 13.2.1 on sm_120.
- VRAM is about 13.2 GiB with q8_0 KV (the 14.3 GiB figure assumed f16).
- About 25.7 GiB in RAM leaves little headroom against the roughly 40 GiB free.
- Prefill may be slow (#25859). Hybrid models get prefix-cache misses (#30357).
- Ranked below Qwen3.6 because AA's TB2.1 for this model (38.2) is below NVIDIA's for Qwen3.6 (44.38), and decode is slower.

Other caveats:

Pick it over rank 2 only if your own testing favours it.

It is the fastest option: about 200 tok/s measured on a desktop RTX 5080. The full 128k context fits, and llama.cpp grammar-enforces tool calls. Agentic strength is weak, though. ranking.reason:
This is the best fully-vLLM option, and it matches the user's vLLM-first preference with the full 262k context in VRAM and an inferred bound near 166 tok/s. The placement rests only on vendor claims: SWE-V 70.6 and TB2.1 46.2 are extraordinary for a 9B model, and the org is unverified and anonymous. Its base, Qwen3.5-9B, scores about 53 on SWE-V in other vendors' tables.

Corrections and caveats:
- With FP8 KV, attention runs on FlashInfer or Triton, not FA2.
- #54331 was reproduced on sm_120 with FP8 KV under load in the sister model. Use --enforce-eager or BF16 KV at 131k if crashes appear.
- The LICENSE link returns 404.

notes:
Ranking weights independent evidence first: Artificial Analysis (AA), NVIDIA's same-harness table in the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning card, and the SWE-bench leaderboard. Vendor numbers count only as secondary evidence. Ranks 5, 6 and 10 rest only on vendor claims.

Runtime choice and image corrections:
- Eight of the top ten run best on llama.cpp. On this 16 GB card in vLLM v0.33.0, nothing above about 14 GiB fits, and UVA expert offload is undone for Marlin-repacked MoE weights (#66264). That refutes every vLLM offload plan in the records: AWQ Qwen3-Coder-30B, GLM AutoRound, Lightning NVFP4 and Laguna NVFP4.
- Use ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 (CUDA 12.8.1). The b12418 image tag does not exist. :server-cuda13 sets NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA cuda>=13.5 with no GeForce brand clause, so it may not start on this GeForce card with its CUDA 13.2 driver. It also hits the IQ-quant nvcc 13.2 miscompile concern (#28581).
- Add GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 on this laptop (#27330, reproduced on driver 595.99.02).
- Every speed figure is inferred from bandwidth. Nothing has been measured on this RTX 5080 Laptop. Measure the 15 tok/s floor on the q8_0-KV configurations first (#27623).

OpenCode setup: use a custom provider with capabilities.tools set to true. Built-in vLLM discovery disables tools. Set reasoningField to 'reasoning' for vLLM and 'reasoning_content' for llama.cpp.

Family coverage:
- Qwen: ranks 1-3.
- Gemma: rank 4. Gemma 4 12B on vLLM is the vLLM-native Gemma alternate (AA TB2.1 27.3%).
- Nemotron: rank 8. Nano 4B and Bolt E4B are too weak for coding agents. Bolt E4B is capped at exactly 64k.
- OpenAI: rank 9. gpt-oss-120b is excluded because it needs about 49-52 GiB of RAM against about 40 GiB free.
- DeepSeek: no runnable DeepSeek model qualifies. DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B has no working tool calling (AA tau2 0%, Terminal-Bench Hard 1.5%), so list it only under 'thinking, no tools'.

Lists by thinking and tool calling:
- No thinking, with tools: Qwen3-Coder-Next (rank 3); Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B and Devstral Small 2 are not ranked. Devstral reaches only 32k at q8_0 KV; 64k needs q4_0 KV or 3-bit weights. Its independent mini-SWE-agent score is 56.4. Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B is older, scoring 31.8 on SWE-V in Kwaipilot's independent same-harness run.
- Always-on thinking, with tools: gpt-oss-20b.
- Thinking toggle, with tools: everything else.

Also excluded: Qwen3.5-9B, MiMo-V2.6-Distill (vendor-only SFT), Granite 4.2 8B (AA index 5.1) and Ministral 3 (AA TB2.1 9.7%), all weaker than ranks 1-10. MiMo's tool-call argument format is also contested.

No browsing was done. All facts come from the provided verification and challenge records.
